claims.text: Conventional ordered multi-metal spinel oxide automotive exhaust catalysts require relatively high PGM loadings.
Controlled doping can promote a statistically disordered cation distribution in multi-metal spinel oxides.
Rapid quenching can promote a statistically disordered cation distribution in multi-metal spinel oxides.
Greater configurational disorder increases the oxygen-vacancy concentration in the spinel oxide.
Greater configurational disorder diversifies the catalyst's surface active sites.
A disordered cation arrangement increases the density of active sites.
A disordered cation arrangement increases the accessibility of active sites.
A disordered cation arrangement facilitates oxygen mobility.
A disordered cation arrangement improves catalyst redox dynamics.
The proposed active-site and oxygen-transport effects improve catalytic conversion of exhaust gases.
The proposed disorder-mediated effects improve catalyst durability.
Improved activity and durability permit reduced PGM usage.
Under automotive exhaust conditions, highly disordered spinel catalysts will have higher conversion efficiency than conventionally ordered catalysts even with lower PGM loading.
Under automotive exhaust conditions, highly disordered spinel catalysts will retain performance longer than conventionally ordered catalysts even with lower PGM loading.
The magnitude of the performance gain depends on the particular combination of metals.
The magnitude of the performance gain depends on the degree of configurational disorder achieved.

contradictions.description: The stated baseline uses traditional PGM loading, and the predicted outcome implies comparison against that conventional baseline, but the experiment assigns reduced PGM loading to both ordered and disordered catalysts. It therefore does not directly test performance against the stated traditional-loading baseline.

The falsification rule treats inferior performance caused by reduced PGM loading as decisive, but the design includes no traditional-PGM-loading control, so the effect of lowering PGM cannot be isolated.
